summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Pinetree through the Eval & Quality Monitoring capabilities (prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons) in Redwood Optimize and Console. Customer liked prompt-set based regression alerts and per-prompt diagnostics; primary concerns were data residency, audit logs, and false positive alert noise. Agreed next steps: trial access, share security docs, run 1-week eval with customer prompt set and schedule throughput benchmark.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Gomez (Pinetree Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Eng Manager), Priya Shah (Data Privacy)

Summary: quick walkthrough of Redwood's Eval & Quality Monitoring (Optimize + Console) with focus on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for making time, i'm Jordan with Redwood, i lead the AE for retail. quick roundtable?
[00:05] Aisha: hi, aisha here. head of ml at pinetree. excited to see the quality monitoring stuff, we have a lot of prompt drift concerns.
[00:08] Marcus: Marcus, eng lead. primarily interested in throughput and how noisy alerts are.
[00:11] Priya: Priya, privacy/compliance. i'll be asking about retention and audit logs.
[00:13] Jordan: awesome. samir is our se, he'll do the demo. samir over to you.

[00:30] Samir: thanks jordan. i'll share my screen — starting with the Optimize dashboard. note: sometimes the share overlay lags, so bear with me.
[00:42] Samir: first concept is prompt sets — you upload a labeled set of prompts representative of your traffic, we run evals against a baseline and any candidate models. you can attach severity labels and acceptance criteria per-prompt.
[00:58] Aisha: when you say attach acceptance criteria, do you mean thresholds on metrics like exact match? or custom metrics?
[01:05] Samir: both. default metrics include semantic similarity (embedding-based), token-level metrics, and custom rubric scores. you can also plug in your own scoring function via the SDK — for example, a custom hallucination check. we run the evals and surface per-prompt scores and an aggregate baseline.
[01:20] Marcus: are these evals run on our data in a private env? i'm sensitive about sending PII to hosted infra.
[01:26] Samir: good question. for Hosted mode we can run evals in our infra with encryption; for Dedicated/Private we can run the evals on your VPC or on-prem package. there's an option in the console to select eval execution environment. note: in hosted we strip payloads if requested and we have KMS integration.
[01:40] Priya: can you show audit logs for eval runs? we need traceability for each dataset used.
[01:44] Samir: yes — audit log tab shows who triggered the eval, prompt set id, model version, and sha of scoring script. we also persist evaluation artifacts for configurable retention windows.

[02:10] Samir: demo: upload a prompt set — here i'm uploading a CSV (slight delay) — columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output, severity. the UI also supports drag/drop and API upload.
[02:32] Jordan: the API example in the docs shows python snippet using redwood.optimize.upload_prompt_set(), just fyi, i'll share that link after.
[02:40] Aisha: okay do you support dynamic prompt templates? we have parameterized prompts in prod.
[02:45] Samir: yes you can store templates with placeholders; the eval runner expands them with example slots. we also do per-slot masking so you can separate PII tokens.

[03:15] Samir: next: regression alerts. once you baseline a model, we run periodic evals or on-deploy evals. if aggregate or per-prompt scores fall beyond a configured delta, the system fires an alert — you can set severity and notification channels (slack, email, webhook).
[03:35] Marcus: how do you avoid alert fatigue? if i have 10k prompts, i don't want 5k alerts.
[03:40] Samir: two built-in controls: noise threshold (min sample size and delta) and grouped alerts — we group by prompt clusters using embeddings similarity. also you can configure per-prompt thresholds and only monitor a subset as a canary set.
[03:55] Aisha: does grouping ever mis-cluster? i've seen similar prompts with different expected outputs get grouped.
[04:00] Samir: occasionally; clustering is configurable. you can override cluster membership manually. we tag clusters and provide adjacency views so you can inspect false grouping — we annotate with example tokens.
[04:12] Marcus: is there an auto rollback for canary fail?
[04:15] Samir: you can wire alerts to rollout policies — e.g., automatic pause/rollback if regression > X on canary. works with model pinning in Deploy.

[04:40] Jordan: quick pause — any Qs on metric types?
[04:44] Aisha: what about A/B comparisons — we run two models in prod for a week and want to compare quality.
[04:50] Samir: yep the A/B comparison tool lets you define cohorts and period, then compute per-prompt and aggregate deltas. we support statistical significance tests (bootstrap CIs) and show per-prompt scatter plots. you can filter by traffic slice (region, route, user segment).
[05:10] Aisha: nice. can we compare across quantized variants? like 4-bit vs 8-bit?
[05:14] Samir: yes — model variants are first-class. the dashboard shows latency, cost, and quality tradeoffs side-by-side.

[05:35] [08:00] Speaker 1: (murmur) — some chatter about internal rollout cadence
[08:10] Samir: going to show an example alert — this was a real customer case where a generation mode change caused a spike in hallucination score. you can see the per-prompt timeline and the example output diffs. note: transcription in the sample may show 'KV cash' which is actually KV cache, small transcription hiccup.
[08:30] Aisha: in the diffs, can you see token-level attention?
[08:34] Samir: we don't surface raw attention weights, but we show delta tokens and similarity heatmaps. for debug you can download the raw outputs and run local analysis.

[09:00] Marcus: what's the expected cost for running weekly evals on 50k prompts? rough ballpark.
[09:08] Samir: depends on model size and eval depth. Optimize has options: light eval (embedding similarity) vs heavy eval (full generation + rubric scoring). ballpark: light eval is an order of magnitude cheaper. we can run a sample estimate once you share prompt set size.
[09:25] Jordan: we'll include a cost estimate in follow-up; also the pricing sheet has per-eval rates and discounts for Dedicated.

[10:00] Aisha: i'm curious about A/B experiment instrumentation. do we need to route traffic through Redwood or can we supply logs?
[10:06] Samir: two modes: server-side routing — Redwood SDK can split traffic and capture responses — or ingest logs via S3/CSV. both feed into the A/B comparison. server-side gives more real-time metrics.
[10:18] Priya: about logs — can we keep logs within our VPC?
[10:22] Samir: with Private you can keep artifacts in your S3 and we only store pointers; with Dedicated we can configure retention to comply with your policies.

[11:00] Jordan: security quickfire — soc2, iso?
[11:04] Samir: we are SOC2 compliant; we have KMS integration, SSO/SAML, RBAC. i'll send the security pack.
[11:12] Priya: need details on redaction and prompt hashing for PII — do you support deterministic hashing?
[11:18] Samir: yes, you can choose hashing at ingestion and optionally redact or tokenize. the SDK also supports client-side PII scrubbing.

[12:30] Samir: walking through the Console: per-route dashboard, per-prompt drilldown. here's a prompt set view: top failing prompts, histogram of similarity scores, and example diffs. notice the alert timeline on the right.
[12:50] Marcus: can i export failing prompts as a CSV for engineering triage?
[12:54] Samir: yes export button; also webhook to push failing prompts to backlog.

[14:00] Aisha: about false positives in regression alerts — can we set grace windows? sometimes an upstream change causes transient spikes.
[14:08] Samir: we support grace window and minimum evaluation count before flagging. also aggregated alerts only trigger after consecutive failures beyond threshold.

[15:00] [20:00] Samir: shows an A/B comparison example — scatter plot of prompt-level delta vs impression count; highlight the top 10 where one model regressed. demo shows tagging those for follow-up.
[20:30] Aisha: will the dashboard annotate the cause guess? like model change vs tokenization change?
[20:36] Samir: we provide heuristic annotations — e.g., large tokenization deltas flagged as probable tokenizer or prompt-template change. it's a heuristic, not guaranteed.

[21:00] Marcus: instrumenting our infra — how quickly can we get a trial of Optimize?
[21:05] Jordan: we can spin up a 30-day trial account today; we'll give access to the Optimize dashboard and a sandbox eval runner.
[21:15] Priya: what data will be stored by default in the trial?
[21:20] Jordan: default is 30-day retention for artifacts in trial. we can change retention or enable no-persist for sensitive tests.

[22:00] Samir: demo: uploading a small prompt set and running a quick eval — showing per-prompt heatmap, similarity score, and a rubric pass/fail. note: the sample eval uses embedding-based similarity with cosine threshold 0.78.
[22:25] Aisha: can we define multi-metric alerts? like require both similarity drop and increased toxicity?
[22:30] Samir: yes — alert rules support boolean combinations (AND/OR) across metrics. you can set severity and notification routing per rule.

[23:00] Jordan: potential integration with our canary release flow — we can attach a rollout policy to a model variant and tie it to an alert rule.
[23:10] Marcus: good. do we have an API for starting rollbacks?
[23:14] Samir: yes, Deploy API supports model pin/unpin and rollback endpoints; you can automate via webhook from Optimize.

[24:00] Aisha: small nit — in the UI i noticed a label that said 'Optimize' spelled 'Optima' in one of our screenshots last week, is that a branding mismatch?
[24:08] Jordan: lol, thanks, we'll fix that asset. sometimes the PDF export truncates names.

[25:00] [30:00] Samir: now touching on evaluation artifacts — we store the model outputs, embeddings, and computed scores; you can delete or export. we also support storing only hashes for compliance.
[30:20] Priya: if we keep only hashes, can we still run detailed diffs later?
[30:25] Samir: not without raw outputs; hashes allow you to verify run consistency but not reconstruct outputs. we recommend keeping raw outputs for short windows and hashes thereafter.

[31:00] Marcus: timeline: we want to run a pilot in July and potential Dedicated discussion in August.
[31:06] Jordan: sounds reasonable — pilot: 1-week eval on real traffic with canary set + benchmark.

[32:15] Samir: i'll coordinate the benchmark; for throughput we'll run token/sec on your typical payload sizes and show cost per 1M tokens.

[33:00] Aisha: any limitations on languages? we run english and Spanish.
[33:05] Samir: supported. some metrics like exact-match are language-agnostic; semantic similarity uses multilingual embeddings.

[34:00] Jordan: recap & next steps — jordan: we'll send trial access and the security pack; samir: will run 1-week eval and schedule benchmark; priya: share retention constraints.
[34:15] Aisha: can we have a short training for our data team on how to set thresholds?
[34:18] Samir: yes, we'll set a 45-minute workshop.

[35:00] Marcus: questions on pricing and discounts? jordan: we'll follow up with pricing sheet and sample cost estimate.

[36:00] Priya: thanks, that's helpful. one more ask — we need to see the SOC2 cert and pen test summary.
[36:06] Jordan: will include in security pack.

[37:00] [43:00] Jordan: okay thanks everyone. final notes: i'll send a follow-up email with links to the docs: 1) Optimize quickstart, 2) API examples for prompt set upload, 3) security pack, and 4) schedule link for the benchmark. expect the trial invite by end of day.
[43:30] Aisha: thanks, really like the per-prompt diagnostics.
[43:35] Marcus: appreciate the grouping/cluster features.
[43:40] Priya: thanks, talk soon.
[43:45] Jordan: bye all.

END TRANSCRIPT

Referenced artifacts/links:
- Optimize quickstart (link sent in follow-up)
- security-pack/soc2.pdf (to be shared)
- sample prompt_set.csv (demo upload)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard tokens (e.g., KV cache -> KV cash) and speaker overlaps.
